          - generic [ref=f84e7927]:
            - heading "Allocation behavior" [level=4] [ref=f84e7928]
            - paragraph [ref=f84e7929]:
              - text: In general
              - code [ref=f84e7930]: Vec
              - text: does not guarantee any particular growth or allocation strategy. That also applies to this trait impl.
            - paragraph [ref=f84e7931]:
              - strong [ref=f84e7932]: "Note:"
              - text: This section covers implementation details and is therefore exempt from stability guarantees.
            - paragraph [ref=f84e7933]: "Vec may use any or none of the following strategies, depending on the supplied iterator:"
            - list [ref=f84e7934]:
              - listitem [ref=f84e7935]:
                - text: preallocate based on
                - link [ref=f84e7936] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: ../iter/trait.Iterator.html#method.size_hint
                  - code [ref=f84e7937]: Iterator::size_hint()
                - list [ref=f84e7938]:
                  - listitem [ref=f84e7939]: and panic if the number of items is outside the provided lower/upper bounds
              - listitem [ref=f84e7940]:
                - text: use an amortized growth strategy similar to
                - code [ref=f84e7941]: pushing
                - text: one item at a time
              - listitem [ref=f84e7942]: perform the iteration in-place on the original allocation backing the iterator
            - paragraph [ref=f84e7943]:
              - text: The last case warrants some attention. It is an optimization that in many cases reduces peak memory consumption and improves cache locality. But when big, short-lived allocations are created, only a small fraction of their items get collected, no further use is made of the spare capacity and the resulting
              - code [ref=f84e7944]: Vec
              - text: is moved into a longer-lived structure, then this can lead to the large allocations having their lifetimes unnecessarily extended which can result in increased memory footprint.
            - paragraph [ref=f84e7945]:
              - text: In cases where this is an issue, the excess capacity can be discarded with
              - link [ref=f84e7946] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: struct.Vec.html#method.shrink_to
                - code [ref=f84e7947]: Vec::shrink_to()
              - text: ","
              - link [ref=f84e7948] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: struct.Vec.html#method.shrink_to_fit
                - code [ref=f84e7949]: Vec::shrink_to_fit()
              - text: or by collecting into
              - link [ref=f84e7950] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: ../boxed/struct.Box.html
                - code [ref=f84e7951]: Box<[T]>
              - text: instead, which additionally reduces the size of the long-lived struct.
            - code [ref=f84e7954]: "static LONG_LIVED: Mutex<Vec<Vec<u16>>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new()); for i in 0..10 { let big_temporary: Vec<u16> = (0..1024).collect(); // discard most items let mut result: Vec<_> = big_temporary.into_iter().filter(|i| i % 100 == 0).collect(); // without this a lot of unused capacity might be moved into the global result.shrink_to_fit(); LONG_LIVED.lock().unwrap().push(result); }"

              - generic [ref=f84e8101]:
                - paragraph [ref=f84e8102]: Creates a consuming iterator, that is, one that moves each value out of the vector (from start to end). The vector cannot be used after calling this.
                - heading "Examples" [level=5] [ref=f84e8103]
                - code [ref=f84e8106]: "let v = vec![\"a\".to_string(), \"b\".to_string()]; let mut v_iter = v.into_iter(); let first_element: Option<String> = v_iter.next(); assert_eq!(first_element, Some(\"a\".to_string())); assert_eq!(v_iter.next(), Some(\"b\".to_string())); assert_eq!(v_iter.next(), None);"

                  - code [ref=f84e8942]: Vec<T>
                  - text: as an array, if its size exactly matches that of the requested array.

                  - text: If the length doesn’t match, the input comes back in
                  - code [ref=f84e8948]: Err
                  - text: ":"

                - paragraph [ref=f84e8952]:
                  - text: If you’re fine with just getting a prefix of the
